messages.subject: add some points in geom_line
parts:
Hi everyone,

I want to add big, red, and triangle points when am == 1 in following graph

mtcars$carb <- factor(mtcars$carb)
qplot(wt, mpg, data = mtcars, colour = carb) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = carb, linetype = carb))

I tried,

+  geom_point(data= mtcars, aes(wt[am==1], mpg[am==1]),colour="red",shape="triangle", size=20)

but it gives me an error message.

Error in data.frame(x = c(2.62, 2.875, 2.32, 2.2, 1.615, 1.835, 1.935,  : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 13, 32

Could you help me in this matter?

Thank you ahead.

Sincerely,
Soyeon

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: add some points in geom_line
parts:
On 9/16/2013 1:19 PM, Sophia wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I want to add big, red, and triangle points when am == 1 in following graph
>
> mtcars$carb <- factor(mtcars$carb)
> qplot(wt, mpg, data = mtcars, colour = carb) +
> geom_line(aes(group = carb, linetype = carb))
>
> I tried,
>
> + geom_point(data= mtcars, aes(wt[am==1],
> mpg[am==1]),colour="red",shape="triangle", size=20)
>
> but it gives me an error message.
>
> Error in data.frame(x = c(2.62, 2.875, 2.32, 2.2, 1.615, 1.835, 1.935, :
> arguments imply differing number of rows: 13, 32
>
> Could you help me in this matter?

When subsetting, subset the data, not the aesthetics. The aesthetics
show which variables should be associated with what visual element.
Also, shape 2 is a triangle; using "triangle" just uses the "t" as the
symbol.

geom_line(aes(group = carb, linetype = carb)) +
geom_point(data= mtcars[mtcars$am==1,],
colour="red", shape=2, size=20)

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.subject: Re: add some points in geom_line
parts:
On 9/16/2013 2:05 PM, Soyeon Kim wrote:
> Thank your detailed explanation!
> One more question. How to fill the triangles with red color?

Solid triangles are shape 17, solid triangles which can be filled with a
different color are shape 24. See the last plot on
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/aes_linetype_size_shape.html for the
different shapes that are available. Or, as an alternative look at the
chart created by:

ggplot(data.frame(x = 1, y = 1, z = 0:25), aes(x = x, y = y)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = z), size = 10, colour = "Red", fill =
"lightblue") +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(1)) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(1)) +
scale_shape_identity() +
facet_wrap(~z) +
theme_bw() +
theme(axis.text = element_blank(),
axis.title = element_blank(),
axis.ticks = element_blank())
